response.sql: WITH cat AS (SELECT category, AVG(remaining) AS avg_remaining, SUM(amount - spent) AS total FROM budget WHERE amount > 75 GROUP BY category), overall AS (SELECT AVG(total) AS avg_total FROM cat) SELECT cat.category, cat.avg_remaining, cat.total, cat.total - overall.avg_total AS amount_above_overall_avg FROM cat CROSS JOIN overall WHERE cat.total > overall.avg_total;

assumptions.assumption: Budget rows with NULL category form one group together, since GROUP BY treats NULLs as equal. Rows with amount NULL are excluded by the amount > 75 filter.

Missing values are handled per measure: AVG(remaining) skips NULL remaining values, and SUM(amount - spent) skips rows where amount or spent is NULL. A category whose total is NULL is left out of the overall average and cannot pass the strict comparison.
